project.name: mern-chat-pwa
project.mission: Build and deploy a polished MERN stack real-time chat PWA within nine days to demonstrate full-stack engineering ability, React competency, Node/Express API design, MongoDB schema modeling, Socket.IO real-time communication, authentication, authorization, deployment discipline, and interview-ready technical communication.
project.positioning: A real-time team chat PWA built with MongoDB, Express, React, Node, Socket.IO, JWT authentication, role-based workspace/channel access, and MongoDB message persistence.

repositoryLayout.reason: Keep the React client, Node/Express server, and custom UI component library isolated in their own top-level directories while sharing one repository for planning and coordinated delivery.

constraints.description: No voice chat in the nine-day MVP.
constraints.reason: Protect scope and keep the interview build focused on reliable text-chat flows.

constraints.description: No video chat in the nine-day MVP.
constraints.reason: Audio/video infrastructure would dilute delivery time for the core full-stack demonstration.

constraints.description: No screen sharing in the nine-day MVP.
constraints.reason: RTC features are out of scope for a polished interview MVP.

constraints.description: No direct messages in the nine-day MVP.
constraints.reason: Workspace and channel collaboration is the primary demo path.

constraints.description: No message reactions in the nine-day MVP.
constraints.reason: Focus on durable message creation, retrieval, and real-time delivery first.

constraints.description: No file uploads in the nine-day MVP.
constraints.reason: Uploads add storage, validation, and security complexity with limited interview payoff.

constraints.description: No image uploads in the nine-day MVP.
constraints.reason: The MVP should showcase chat fundamentals over asset handling.

constraints.description: No advanced permissions matrix in the nine-day MVP.
constraints.reason: Owner/member roles are sufficient to demonstrate authorization discipline.

constraints.description: No push notifications in the nine-day MVP.
constraints.reason: Push infrastructure is secondary to installability and offline fallback.

constraints.description: No bots in the nine-day MVP.
constraints.reason: The interview value comes from core product flows rather than automation features.

constraints.description: No threads in the nine-day MVP.
constraints.reason: Nested message hierarchy would complicate the schema and UI unnecessarily.

constraints.description: No end-to-end encryption in the nine-day MVP.
constraints.reason: Security posture should be honest and appropriately scoped for a fast portfolio build.

constraints.description: No complex moderation system in the nine-day MVP.
constraints.reason: The demo should emphasize collaboration primitives and server-side authorization.

constraints.description: Position the product as Discord-inspired or team-chat inspired, not a full Discord replacement.
constraints.reason: Clear framing avoids overselling scope and improves interview credibility.

qualityGates.name: Authorization is enforced server-side
criteria: Users cannot access workspaces they do not belong to
Users cannot access channels in unauthorized workspaces
Socket events validate membership before joining rooms

qualityGates.name: Real-time messaging works
criteria: Messages broadcast to active channel members
Channel switching does not leak messages
Reconnect does not create duplicate listeners

qualityGates.name: Deployment is interview-ready
criteria: Server is deployed on the droplet
MongoDB Community is installed and reachable on the droplet
Nginx is configured for the app and API

architecturePrinciples.name: Polished vertical slice over broad clone
architecturePrinciples.description: The project should demonstrate a complete, deployed, reliable MVP rather than a wide but unfinished Discord clone.

architecturePrinciples.name: Server-side authorization is mandatory
architecturePrinciples.description: All workspace, channel, message, and socket access must be validated on the backend.

architecturePrinciples.name: Persist first, broadcast second
architecturePrinciples.description: Messages should be saved successfully before being broadcast to other clients.

architecturePrinciples.name: Deployment is part of the product
architecturePrinciples.description: The app is not interview-ready until it can be accessed through a public URL and demonstrated from a clean account.

architecturePrinciples.name: Every feature needs a demo path
architecturePrinciples.description: Features that cannot be shown clearly in a five-minute interview demo should be cut or deferred.

architecturePrinciples.name: Separate frontend, server, and UI library project directories
architecturePrinciples.description: The React app should live under frontend/, the Node/Express app should live under server/, and the shared component library should live under ui/ so toolchains, env files, and reusable presentation code stay cleanly separated.

architecturePrinciples.name: Single-droplet deployment should stay operationally simple
architecturePrinciples.description: Deploy the built frontend and the Node server to one Ubuntu droplet behind Nginx, with MongoDB Community installed on the same host, so the MVP remains easy to operate and explain.

architecturePrinciples.name: Test-driven development with full coverage
architecturePrinciples.description: Both frontend and server changes should be driven by automated tests, and the repository should maintain 100% coverage for the code currently under test.

risks.title: Scope creep
risks.mitigation: Keep the MVP limited to auth, workspaces, channels, persisted real-time messages, PWA installability, and deployment.

risks.title: Real-time complexity delays deployment
risks.mitigation: Implement REST-based message persistence first, then layer Socket.IO broadcasting over the working persistence path.

risks.title: Deployment issues consume final day
risks.mitigation: Deploy a skeleton version early, then continuously deploy improvements.

risks.title: Overbuilding UI instead of core functionality
risks.mitigation: Use a simple, clean Discord-inspired layout and prioritize working flows over custom visual complexity.

risks.title: Authorization gaps
risks.mitigation: Validate workspace membership and owner-only actions on the backend and in socket handlers, not only in the UI.

decisions.title: Project scope is a Discord-inspired real-time chat MVP
decisions.summary: Build a serious team-chat vertical slice rather than attempting a full Discord clone.

decisions.title: Socket.IO is the real-time transport for the MVP
decisions.summary: Use Socket.IO rooms and reconnection support to deliver practical real-time messaging in a short timeline.

decisions.title: JWT plus bcrypt is the authentication strategy
decisions.summary: JWT-backed auth with bcrypt hashing is sufficient for this interview-focused MVP and easy to explain.

decisions.title: Use a single DigitalOcean droplet for MVP deployment
decisions.summary: Use a single Ubuntu droplet on DigitalOcean with Nginx and MongoDB Community to keep deployment simple, cheap, and easy to explain.

interviewTalkingPoints.title: What the project is
interviewTalkingPoints.note: I built a deployed MERN stack real-time chat PWA to demonstrate full-stack application design in the MERN ecosystem. It includes JWT authentication, workspace membership, owner/member authorization, text channels, persisted MongoDB messages, Socket.IO real-time delivery, and PWA installability. I intentionally scoped it as a polished vertical slice so I could show production-minded tradeoffs instead of an unfinished clone.

interviewTalkingPoints.title: How the pieces fit
interviewTalkingPoints.note: React handles the client experience, Express owns APIs and authorization, MongoDB stores the durable state, and Socket.IO handles channel-scoped real-time delivery after persistence succeeds.

interviewTalkingPoints.title: Why this stack
interviewTalkingPoints.note: A JavaScript/TypeScript-friendly stack kept iteration speed high and let me focus on end-to-end product delivery rather than language boundaries.

interviewTalkingPoints.title: Why this real-time approach
interviewTalkingPoints.note: Socket.IO gave me practical room support, reconnection handling, and event semantics that fit a nine-day MVP better than building raw WebSocket infrastructure by hand.

interviewTalkingPoints.title: Security posture
interviewTalkingPoints.note: The MVP uses JWT authentication, bcrypt password hashing, protected routes, and server-side membership checks so authorization does not depend on hidden UI controls.

interviewTalkingPoints.title: Why these collections
interviewTalkingPoints.note: The schema keeps user, workspace, channel, and message data separate while embedding workspace membership to make owner/member authorization checks straightforward.

interviewTalkingPoints.title: Why lightweight PWA features
interviewTalkingPoints.note: I prioritized installability, manifest support, icons, and a basic offline fallback rather than an overly complex offline-first data model.

interviewTalkingPoints.title: Why a single-droplet deployment
interviewTalkingPoints.note: A single DigitalOcean droplet with Nginx and MongoDB Community keeps the deployment topology simple while still demonstrating real Linux server operations and a public production URL.

interviewTalkingPoints.title: What I intentionally cut
interviewTalkingPoints.note: I explicitly cut voice, video, DMs, uploads, reactions, and complex permissions so I could complete a deployed, credible vertical slice.

interviewTalkingPoints.title: Where it could go next
interviewTalkingPoints.note: The next logical steps are presence, typing indicators, message editing, better auth hardening, richer moderation, and deeper offline support.

environmentVariables.name: MONGODB_URI
environmentVariables.description: MongoDB connection string for local development and the MongoDB Community instance installed on the droplet.

environmentVariables.name: JWT_SECRET
environmentVariables.description: Secret used to sign and verify JWTs.

environmentVariables.name: PORT
environmentVariables.description: Internal Node server listen port used behind Nginx on the droplet or by local development.

environmentVariables.name: CORS_ORIGIN
environmentVariables.description: Allowed origin for REST and Socket.IO access; may be the same public domain served by Nginx in production.

environmentVariables.name: VITE_API_BASE_URL
environmentVariables.description: Base URL for REST API requests from the frontend, ideally a same-origin path such as /api in production.

environmentVariables.name: VITE_SOCKET_URL
environmentVariables.description: Optional Socket.IO URL override for the frontend; can be omitted when production uses the same public origin through Nginx.

checklist.item: Provision the DigitalOcean Ubuntu droplet and basic server access
Install MongoDB Community, Node.js, and any process manager needed on the droplet
Build the frontend and make it available from the droplet deployment
Configure Nginx to serve the frontend and proxy API and Socket.IO traffic to the Node server
Configure production environment variables and same-origin CORS strategy
Run smoke test with a fresh account and two sessions
Update README and demo script with live URLs
